results.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
results.proof_sketch: A certificate specifies the locking translation of each domino. For each reconstructed board state, the translations reachable by the current fixed-orientation domino from its prescribed spawn form a polynomial-size, constant-degree graph, including the source's fixed spawn region and loss boundary. Breadth-first search verifies reachability of the certified translation. The verifier then checks that downward movement is blocked, rejects every source-defined loss-causing lock, adds the two cells, and performs deterministic row deletion. A reachable translation always has a simple path, so cyclic movement cannot require a superpolynomial certificate. Repeating for the explicitly listed pieces takes polynomial time.

results.claim: Finite-sequence unrotatable-domino survival is exactly reachability in a finite layered acyclic graph: layer i consists of settled board masks obtainable after the first i prescribed pieces, and an edge represents one source-legal, nonlosing placement and its deterministic row-deletion result.
results.proof_sketch: For layer i and board mask B, form the translation graph for prescribed piece i+1. Its vertices are the collision-free translations of that fixed-orientation domino in the source's bounded board/spawn region; directed edges are exactly the allowed one-unit left, right, and down moves, and the start vertex is the prescribed spawn. Breadth-first search identifies the reachable translations. Retain a reachable translation only when downward motion is blocked and locking there passes the exact source loss test for stage i+1, including its ceiling and next-spawn convention. Cell insertion followed by deterministic simultaneous deletion of all full rows produces a unique mask B'; add (i,B)→(i+1,B'). Every surviving play supplies such an edge at each stage. Conversely, select a witnessing movement path and lock for each edge of any layered path; induction on i shows that the reconstructed board is B, the placement does not lose, and the deterministic update is B'. Thus a path from (0,B0) to layer n exists if and only if all n pieces can be survived. Sequence position and occupancy contain all future-relevant state under the source rules.

results.claim: If A=WH is the explicit board area, the layered-graph reformulation gives an exact deterministic 2^{O(A)}poly(n,A)-time and 2^{O(A)}poly(A)-space algorithm; therefore finite-sequence survival is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by board area.
results.proof_sketch: A settled visible board is an A-bit mask, so a layer contains at most 2^A distinct masks. For each mask, the fixed-orientation translation graph has O(A) vertices and constant degree in the bounded board/spawn region. One breadth-first search finds all reachable locks, and each loss check, insertion, simultaneous row deletion, and successor encoding takes polynomial time in A. Maintain only the deduplicated reachable masks in the current and next layers and repeat for n stages. This uses 2^{O(A)}poly(A) space and 2^{O(A)}poly(n,A) time. By the preceding two-way correspondence, the algorithm accepts exactly the survivable instances. The exponent depends on the unrestricted input board area, so this is not a polynomial-time classification of the general target.

results.claim: For odd board width W, let q be the number of initial rows whose maximal initially empty intervals all have even length. Every surviving play prefix containing V vertical dominoes and deleting R rows satisfies R≤q+2V; the odd-width hypothesis is essential.
results.proof_sketch: Track each initial row and each subsequently introduced empty top row as a token until it is deleted. If an initial token clears without receiving a vertical-domino cell, its initially occupied cells remain barriers and horizontal dominoes must tile every initially empty interval, so the token is one of the q eligible rows. A newly introduced token starts with W empty cells; for odd W it cannot become full using only two-cell horizontal contributions. Thus every other deleted token received a vertical-domino cell. Charge that deletion to one such cell. A vertical domino contributes two cells to two distinct row tokens, and a cell disappears when its token is deleted, so at most 2V deletions can be charged. For even width the conclusion fails: on an empty width-two board, horizontal dominoes repeatedly fill and clear the bottom row with V=0, making R unbounded while q is fixed.

results.claim: Let c_i=Σ_j floor(ℓ_i,j/2), where the ℓ_i,j are the maximal initially empty interval lengths in initial row i, let C=Σ_i c_i, and let f=floor(W/2). If a play prefix places X horizontal dominoes and deletes R rows, then X≤C+fR.
results.proof_sketch: Assign every horizontal domino to the row token containing it. Until initial token i is deleted, its initially occupied cells persist, so every assigned horizontal domino lies wholly inside one of its original empty intervals. Disjointness permits at most floor(ℓ_i,j/2) dominoes in interval j and at most c_i in that token. Each row deletion introduces exactly one new empty width-W token. Such a token can contain at most f disjoint horizontal dominoes before it is deleted or play ends. There are R introduced tokens, so summing the capacities of all initial and introduced tokens gives X≤C+fR. Vertical pieces can occupy or split empty intervals but cannot increase these horizontal capacities.

results.claim: For every odd W, define U=C+q floor(W/2). Every surviving prefix with X horizontal and V vertical dominoes satisfies X≤U+(W−1)V. For odd W≥3, equivalently V≥ceil(max(0,X−U)/(W−1)); hence any prescribed prefix violating this computable inequality makes the instance a NO-instance.
results.proof_sketch: Combine X≤C+fR with R≤q+2V. Because f=floor(W/2)=(W−1)/2 for odd W, X≤C+f(q+2V)=U+(W−1)V. The initial quantities C and q are obtained by scanning the board, and X and V are fixed prefix counts of the prescribed sequence, so every prefix can be tested in polynomial time. The condition is only necessary: when V=0 it becomes the parent's row-capacity bound U, whose insufficiency is witnessed below.

results.claim: The coefficients in the odd-width obstruction are asymptotically sharp: for every odd W≥3, an empty board of height at least four survives the infinite periodic orientation sequence consisting of W−1 horizontal dominoes followed by one vertical domino, with each period restoring the empty board.
results.proof_sketch: Write W=2f+1 and partition the first W−1 columns into f adjacent pairs. Place one horizontal domino in each pair on the bottom row, then one in each pair directly above it. These 2f=W−1 horizontal dominoes fill the bottom two rows except for the final column. Drop the vertical domino into that column; it completes both rows, both clear, and the board becomes empty. Every lock is confined to the bottom two rows. With H≥4 the top two rows remain empty, so every target is reachable through the top corridor and no lock intersects the spawn region. Repeating survives forever. Each period has R=2, V=1, and X=W−1, proving sharpness of both the factor 2 in R≤q+2V and the coefficient W−1 in the horizontal budget.

results.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
results.proof_sketch: Track physical rows as tokens through row deletion and downward shifts. For initial token i, let ℓi,j be the lengths of its maximal initially empty intervals and set ci=Σj floor(ℓi,j/2). Until the token is deleted, its initially occupied cells remain barriers, so every horizontal domino assigned to it lies within one such interval; hence it receives at most ci pieces. It can clear only if all its empty intervals have even length. Let q count initial tokens satisfying this necessary condition and let C=Σi ci. At most q initial tokens clear. Each such deletion introduces an empty width-W token. Because W is odd, a new token retains even occupancy after every horizontal placement, can never become full, and receives at most floor(W/2) pieces. Therefore U=C+q floor(W/2) bounds every play. Moreover U≤2H floor(W/2)=H(W−1), and C and q are computable in O(WH).

results.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
results.proof_sketch: Partition the columns into fixed adjacent pairs. While the top two rows are empty, straight-drop one domino into every pair, restarting if any row clears. Without an earlier clear, each such placement locks immediately above that pair's previous highest occupied cell, strictly below the top row, and equalizes the two column tops. Let T be the greatest resulting pair top and raise every lower pair to T with further straight drops. The empty top-row corridor makes every target reachable, and all locks remain below the top row. Once all pairs reach T, row T is full and clears. Any earlier or final clear shifts the previously empty top row downward and introduces a new empty top row, restoring two empty top rows. Repeating these finite phases survives arbitrarily many pieces.

results.claim: On an initially empty odd-width W×H board, a row-parallel unrotatable-domino play has no row clears and can survive at most H floor(W/2) pieces; this upper bound need not be attained.
results.proof_sketch: Before a first row clear, every row starts with occupancy zero and each horizontal lock increases one row's occupancy by two. Thus every row has even occupancy, whereas a full odd-width row has odd occupancy; a first clear is impossible. With no clears, disjointness permits at most floor(W/2) dominoes per row, proving the upper bound. Equality fails under the source's spawn-lock loss rule. On an empty 3×2 board, one domino can safely lock on the bottom row. Both possible horizontal positions for a second domino overlap the occupied middle column, so the second domino must lock in the top row. Either top-row position intersects either possible adjacent spawn pair and therefore loses. The exact maximum safe length is 1, not 2=H floor(W/2).

results.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
results.proof_sketch: For the 3×3 board top/middle/bottom = .../.#./..., the token bound is U=2. Every width-three horizontal position contains the middle column, so the central obstruction forces the first domino to lock in the top row. Either possible lock intersects either prescribed adjacent spawn pair and loses immediately; the maximum safe length is therefore 0, showing that U is not an attainable-length characterization. For the 3×2 board .../..#, a domino in the two empty bottom cells safely completes and clears that row. The resulting board is empty. By the preceding exact 3×2 analysis, only one further piece can be placed safely, so the original board's maximum safe length is 2. Thus an achieved row clear does not imply indefinite survival.

results.claim: On a stable two-column board, a straight-dropped horizontal domino clears its landing row and restores the identical board; a vertical domino straight-dropped in a column of minimum occupied height leaves, after line clears, height at most max(h,2), where h was the prior height.
results.proof_sketch: Number rows from the bottom and let hL,hR be the highest occupied rows in the two columns, with zero denoting an empty column and h=max(hL,hR). A horizontal domino spans the board, locks in row h+1, fills that row, and clears it; because no old cell was above h, the old board is restored. For a vertical domino choose a column of smaller height a, and let b be the other height. If both heights are zero, it occupies rows 1 and 2. Otherwise a<b, because equality above zero would make the common top row full. If b≥a+2, the new cells at a+1,a+2 do not exceed the old height b, and deletions cannot raise it. If b=a+1, the lower new cell completes row b; deleting that row shifts the upper new cell from b+1 to b, with nothing above it. Thus the post-clear height is at most max(h,2), and every transient lock uses no row above max(h,2)+1.

results.claim: Every stable two-column board of height at least five whose top three rows are empty survives every prescribed finite—and indeed infinite—sequence of unrotatable horizontal and vertical dominoes.
results.proof_sketch: Let h0 be the initial occupied height and B=max(h0,2). The hypotheses give B≤H−3. For every horizontal piece use the state-restoring straight drop; for every vertical piece translate it within the empty top corridor to a column of minimum occupied height and straight-drop it. The preceding invariant inductively keeps every post-clear state at height at most B. The specified translations are reachable because the top two rows remain empty and the chosen target column contains no cell above its recorded height. Every lock uses rows at most B+1≤H−2, below the entire two-row region in which any fixed-orientation domino can spawn. Hence no lock reaches the ceiling or a next-piece spawn cell, even if loss is tested before line deletion. The invariant and spawn clearance are restored after every piece, proving survival for every orientation sequence.

final_writeup:
This remains rigorous partial progress, not a solution of the requested complexity classification. Survival for an explicitly listed finite sequence of fixed-orientation dominoes is in NP by certifying each lock and checking reachability, loss, and deterministic row deletion in polynomial time.

The structural reformulation makes the remaining nondeterminism exact. For each sequence position and settled board mask, construct the polynomial-size translation graph of the next fixed-orientation domino. Connect that state to every board produced by a reachable, downward-blocked, nonlosing lock followed by the source's simultaneous row deletion. Induction in both directions proves that the original instance is survivable exactly when this layered acyclic graph has a path from the initial board to its final layer. With A=WH there are at most 2^A masks per layer, yielding an exact 2^{O(A)}poly(n,A)-time dynamic program and fixed-parameter tractability by board area. This reformulation does not compress the exponentially many masks on arbitrary boards, so it supplies neither a general polynomial-time algorithm nor hardness.

The verified odd-width obstruction remains intact. Let q count initial rows whose initially empty intervals are all even, let C be the sum of their interval-packing capacities over all initial rows, and put U=C+q floor(W/2). For any play prefix with X horizontal pieces, V vertical pieces, and R deleted rows, token parity gives R≤q+2V. Token capacity independently gives X≤C+R floor(W/2). Consequently

X≤U+(W−1)V.

Thus every odd-width instance has a polynomial-time necessary prefix test, and once X exceeds U it requires at least ceil((X−U)/(W−1)) vertical pieces in that prefix. This is not a sufficient characterization: the center-obstructed 3×3 board already fails despite satisfying the V=0 specialization.

The limitation is exact in its asymptotic coefficient. On an empty odd-width board with at least four rows, fill the bottom two rows horizontally except for one common column, then fill that column with a vertical domino. Both rows clear and the empty board returns. This indefinitely repeatable block uses W−1 horizontal pieces per vertical piece and produces two clears per vertical piece. Conversely, odd width is indispensable to the obstruction: on even width, horizontal pieces alone can repeatedly fill and clear rows.

The remaining verified structural results are preserved. All-horizontal odd-width play has the absolute bound U≤H(W−1); all-horizontal even-width play with two empty top rows survives indefinitely; empty odd-width play has no clears and is bounded by H floor(W/2), with nonattainment already on the empty 3×2 board. A stable two-column board with three empty top rows survives every prescribed mixed-orientation sequence.

The exact layered reduction therefore narrows the algorithmic task to compressing or implicitly searching its board-mask layers, while a hardness result would have to encode choices among those reachable masks. Neither step is proved here. The requested P-versus-NP-hard classification remains unresolved, so claimed_resolution remains PARTIAL.
